passages.text: Then some Pharisees and scribes came to Jesus from Jerusalem and asked, “Why do Your disciples break the tradition of the elders? They do not wash their hands before they eat.”
passages.sermon:
Some Pharisees and scribes came to Jesus.
They came from Jerusalem.
They spoke to Jesus.
They asked Jesus a question.
They said, “Why do your disciples break the tradition of the elders?”
They explained their question.
They said, “Your disciples do not wash their hands when they eat bread.”
passages.original: Τότε προσέρχονται τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων Φαρισαῖοι καὶ γραμματεῖς λέγοντες Διὰ τί οἱ μαθηταί σου παραβαίνουσιν τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων οὐ γὰρ νίπτονται τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῶν ὅταν ἄρτον ἐσθίωσιν

passages.text: Jesus replied, “And why do you break the command of God for the sake of your tradition?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees and scribes.
He answered their question.
He said, “Why do you break God’s command?
You do this because of your tradition.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Διὰ τί καὶ ὑμεῖς παραβαίνετε τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ διὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν

passages.text: For God said, ‘Honor your father and mother’ and ‘Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.’
passages.sermon:
God gave a command.
God said, “Honor your father.”
God said, “Honor your mother.”
God also said, “Anyone who curses his father must be put to death.”
God also said, “Anyone who curses his mother must be put to death.”
passages.original: ὁ γὰρ Θεὸς εἶπεν Τίμα τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα καί Ὁ κακολογῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα θανάτῳ τελευτάτω

passages.text: But you say that if anyone says to his father or mother, ‘Whatever you would have received from me is a gift devoted to God,’ he need not honor his father or mother with it. Thus you nullify the word of God for the sake of your tradition.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees and teachers of the law.
He said, "You have your own tradition."
You teach people to say to their father or mother, "Whatever help you would have received from me is a gift devoted to God."
You say that person does not need to honor his father or mother with it.
You set aside the word of God because of your tradition.
You make God's command empty by following your own rules.
passages.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ λέγετε Ὃς ἂν εἴπῃ τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί Δῶρον ὃ ἐὰν ἐξ ἐμοῦ ὠφεληθῇς οὐ μὴ τιμήσει τὸν πατέρα αὐτοῦ ἢ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἠκυρώσατε τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ διὰ τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν

passages.text: You hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied correctly about you: ‘These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the religious leaders.
He called them hypocrites.
Isaiah was a prophet.
Isaiah spoke words from God long ago.
Isaiah’s prophecy described these leaders.
Isaiah said, “These people honor Me with their lips.”
They speak words of respect to God.
But their hearts are far from God.
Their true feelings and desires do not match their words.
They do not truly love or follow God in their hearts.
passages.original: ὑποκριταί καλῶς ἐπροφήτευσεν περὶ ὑμῶν Ἠσαΐας λέγων Ὁ λαὸς οὗτος τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ Ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἀπέχει ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.’”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees and the crowd.
He said, “They worship Me in vain.
They teach human rules as if they are God’s commands.
Their worship does not please God.
They replace God’s truth with man-made teachings.”
passages.original: Μάτην δὲ σέβονταί με Διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: Jesus called the crowd to Him and said, “Listen and understand.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood before the crowd.
He called the people to come to Him.
He spoke to them directly.
He said, “Listen to My words.
Understand what I am saying.”
passages.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν ὄχλον εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἀκούετε καὶ συνίετε

passages.text: A man is not defiled by what enters his mouth, but by what comes out of it.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowd.
Jesus explained what makes a person unclean.
Food that enters a person's mouth does not make that person unclean.
Words that come out of a person's mouth make that person unclean.
passages.original: οὐ τὸ εἰσερχόμενον εἰς τὸ στόμα κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἀλλὰ τὸ ἐκπορευόμενον ἐκ τοῦ στόματος τοῦτο κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον

passages.text: Then the disciples came to Him and said, “Are You aware that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus taught the crowd.
He said important things about what makes a person unclean.
The disciples came to Jesus.
They spoke to Him.
They said, "The Pharisees heard what You said."
"The Pharisees were offended."
passages.original: Τότε προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Οἶδας ὅτι οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἀκούσαντες τὸν λόγον ἐσκανδαλίσθησαν

passages.text: But Jesus replied, “Every plant that My heavenly Father has not planted will be pulled up by its roots.
passages.sermon:
Jesus replied.
He spoke about plants as an example.
He said, “Every plant that my heavenly Father has not planted will be pulled up by its roots.”
God is the heavenly Father.
God plants what is true and right.
Anything not planted by God will be removed completely.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Πᾶσα φυτεία ἣν οὐκ ἐφύτευσεν ὁ Πατήρ μου ὁ οὐράνιος ἐκριζωθήσεται

passages.text: Disregard them! They are blind guides. If a blind man leads a blind man, both will fall into a pit.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about the Pharisees.
He said, "Leave them alone."
The Pharisees are blind guides.
A blind person cannot lead another blind person.
If a blind person leads a blind person, both will fall into a pit.
passages.original: ἄφετε αὐτούς τυφλοί εἰσιν ὁδηγοί τυφλῶν τυφλὸς δὲ τυφλὸν ἐὰν ὁδηγῇ ἀμφότεροι εἰς βόθυνον πεσοῦνται

passages.text: Peter said to Him, “Explain this parable to us.”
passages.sermon: Peter was a disciple of Jesus.\r\nPeter spoke to Jesus.\r\nPeter said, “Explain this parable to us.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν αὐτῷ Φράσον ἡμῖν τὴν παραβολήν ταύτην

passages.text: “Do you still not understand?” Jesus asked.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe asked them a question.\r\nHe said, "Do you still not understand?"
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ἀκμὴν καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀσύνετοί ἐστε

passages.text: “Do you not yet realize that whatever enters the mouth goes into the stomach and then is eliminated?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus asked them a question.
He said, "Do you not yet understand?"
Everything that enters a person's mouth goes into the stomach.
After that, it is eliminated from the body.
passages.original: οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι πᾶν τὸ εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς τὸ στόμα εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν χωρεῖ καὶ εἰς ἀφεδρῶνα ἐκβάλλεται

passages.text: But the things that come out of the mouth come from the heart, and these things defile a man.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus explained what truly defiles a person.
Words come out of a person’s mouth.
These words come from the heart.
The heart is the source of these words.
These things that come from the heart make a person unclean.
passages.original: τὰ δὲ ἐκπορευόμενα ἐκ τοῦ στόματος ἐκ τῆς καρδίας ἐξέρχεται κἀκεῖνα κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον

passages.text: For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, and slander.
passages.sermon:
The heart is the source of a person's inner life.
Evil thoughts come out of the heart.
Murder comes out of the heart.
Adultery comes out of the heart.
Sexual immorality comes out of the heart.
Theft comes out of the heart.
False testimony comes out of the heart.
Slander comes out of the heart.
passages.original: ἐκ γὰρ τῆς καρδίας ἐξέρχονται διαλογισμοὶ πονηροί φόνοι μοιχεῖαι πορνεῖαι κλοπαί ψευδομαρτυρίαι βλασφημίαι

passages.text: These are what defile a man, but eating with unwashed hands does not defile him.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He explained what makes a person unclean.
Evil things that come from the heart defile a person.
These things make a person unclean before God.
Eating food with unwashed hands does not make a person unclean.
passages.original: ταῦτά ἐστιν τὰ κοινοῦντα τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸ δὲ ἀνίπτοις χερσὶν φαγεῖν οὐ κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον

passages.text: Leaving that place, Jesus withdrew to the district of Tyre and Sidon.
passages.sermon: Jesus left that place.\r\nHe went to the region of Tyre and Sidon.\r\n
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐκεῖθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς τὰ μέρη Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος

passages.text: And a Canaanite woman from that region came to Him, crying out, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me! My daughter is miserably possessed by a demon.”
passages.sermon:
A Canaanite woman lived in that region.
She left her home and came to Jesus.
She cried out to Him.
She said, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on me.”
She said, “My daughter is possessed by a demon.”
She said, “My daughter suffers greatly.”
passages.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ Χαναναία ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων ἐκείνων ἐξελθοῦσα ἔκραζεν λέγουσα Ἐλέησόν με Κύριε υἱὸς Δαυίδ ἡ θυγάτηρ μου κακῶς δαιμονίζεται

passages.text: But Jesus did not answer a word. So His disciples came and urged Him, “Send her away, for she keeps crying out after us.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus did not say anything to the woman.
His disciples came to Him.
They urged Him to send the woman away.
They said, “She keeps crying out after us.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ οὐκ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῇ λόγον καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἠρώτουν αὐτὸν λέγοντες Ἀπόλυσον αὐτήν ὅτι κράζει ὄπισθεν ἡμῶν

passages.text: He answered, “I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the woman.
He answered her.
He said, “God sent me.”
He said, “God sent me only to the lost sheep.”
He said, “The lost sheep are the people of Israel.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Οὐκ ἀπεστάλην εἰ μὴ εἰς τὰ πρόβατα τὰ ἀπολωλότα οἴκου Ἰσραήλ

passages.text: The woman came and knelt before Him. “Lord, help me!” she said.
passages.sermon: A woman came to Jesus.\r\nShe knelt before Him.\r\nShe said, “Lord, help me!”
passages.original: Ἡ δὲ ἐλθοῦσα προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγουσα Κύριε βοήθει μοι

passages.text: But Jesus replied, “It is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the woman.
He replied to her request.
He said, "It is not right to take the bread meant for the children.
It is not right to throw this bread to the dogs."
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Οὐκ ἔστιν καλὸν λαβεῖν τὸν ἄρτον τῶν τέκνων καὶ βαλεῖν τοῖς κυναρίοις

passages.text: “Yes, Lord,” she said, “even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master’s table.”
passages.sermon:
A woman spoke to Jesus.
She said, “Yes, Lord.”
She said, “Even the dogs eat the crumbs.”
She said, “The crumbs fall from their master’s table.”
passages.original: Ἡ δὲ εἶπεν Ναί κύριε καὶ γὰρ τὰ κυνάρια ἐσθίει ἀπὸ τῶν ψιχίων τῶν πιπτόντων ἀπὸ τῆς τραπέζης τῶν κυρίων αὐτῶν

passages.text: “O woman,” Jesus answered, “your faith is great! Let it be done for you as you desire.” And her daughter was healed from that very hour.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the woman.
He said, “Woman, you have great faith.”
He said, “Let it happen for you as you want.”
Her daughter was healed at that moment.
passages.original: Τότε ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῇ Ὦ γύναι μεγάλη σου ἡ πίστις γενηθήτω σοι ὡς θέλεις καὶ ἰάθη ἡ θυγάτηρ αὐτῆς ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης

passages.text: Moving on from there, Jesus went along the Sea of Galilee. Then He went up on a mountain and sat down.
passages.sermon:
Jesus left that place.
He traveled along the Sea of Galilee.
He went up on a mountain.
He sat down there.
passages.original: Καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἦλθεν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ ἀναβὰς εἰς τὸ ὄρος ἐκάθητο ἐκεῖ

passages.text: Large crowds came to Him, bringing the lame, the blind, the crippled, the mute, and many others, and laid them at His feet, and He healed them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus sat on a mountain near the Sea of Galilee.
Many people gathered around Jesus.
These people formed large crowds.
They brought others with them who needed help.
Some of these were lame.
Some were crippled.
Some were blind.
Some were mute.
They also brought many others who were sick or suffering.
They placed these people at the feet of Jesus.
Jesus healed all of them.
passages.original: καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἔχοντες μεθ’ ἑαυτῶν χωλούς κυλλούς τυφλούς κωφούς καὶ ἑτέρους πολλούς καὶ ἔρριψαν αὐτοὺς παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς

passages.text: The crowd was amazed when they saw the mute speaking, the crippled restored, the lame walking, and the blind seeing. And they glorified the God of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Jesus healed many people.
He healed the mute.
The mute began to speak.
He healed the crippled.
The crippled became healthy.
He healed the lame.
The lame began to walk.
He healed the blind.
The blind began to see.
The crowd saw these things.
The crowd was amazed.
The crowd glorified the God of Israel.
passages.original: ὥστε τὸν ὄχλον θαυμάσαι βλέποντας κωφοὺς λαλοῦντας κυλλοὺς ὑγιεῖς καὶ χωλοὺς περιπατοῦντας καὶ τυφλοὺς βλέποντας καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν Θεὸν Ἰσραήλ

passages.text: Then Jesus called His disciples to Him and said, “I have compassion for this crowd, because they have already been with Me three days and have nothing to eat. I do not want to send them away hungry, or they may faint along the way.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw a large crowd.
Jesus called His disciples to Him.
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, "I have compassion for this crowd."
Jesus explained, "These people have been with Me for three days."
Jesus said, "They have nothing to eat."
Jesus said, "I do not want to send them away hungry."
Jesus said, "If I send them away hungry, they may faint on the way."
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν Σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον ὅτι ἤδη ἡμέραι τρεῖς προσμένουσίν μοι καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν τί φάγωσιν καὶ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτοὺς νήστεις οὐ θέλω μή‿ ποτε ἐκλυθῶσιν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ

passages.text: The disciples replied, “Where in this desolate place could we find enough bread to feed such a large crowd?”
passages.sermon:
The disciples spoke to Jesus.
They asked Him a question.
They said, “We are in a desolate place.
Where can we find enough bread here?
How can we feed such a large crowd?”
passages.original: Καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταί Πόθεν ἡμῖν ἐν ἐρημίᾳ ἄρτοι τοσοῦτοι ὥστε χορτάσαι ὄχλον τοσοῦτον

passages.text: “How many loaves do you have?” Jesus asked. “Seven,” they replied, “and a few small fish.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He asked them a question.
Jesus said, “How many loaves do you have?”
The disciples answered Him.
They said, “We have seven loaves.”
They also said, “We have a few small fish.”
passages.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Πόσους ἄρτους ἔχετε Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Ἑπτά καὶ ὀλίγα ἰχθύδια

passages.text: And He instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the crowd.\r\nHe told them to sit down.\r\nHe told them to sit on the ground.
passages.original: Καὶ παραγγείλας τῷ ὄχλῳ ἀναπεσεῖν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν

passages.text: Taking the seven loaves and the fish, He gave thanks and broke them. Then He gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the people.
passages.sermon:
Jesus took the seven loaves and the fish.
He gave thanks to God.
He broke the loaves and the fish.
He gave the food to the disciples.
The disciples gave the food to the people.
passages.original: ἔλαβεν τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς ἰχθύας καὶ εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις

passages.text: They all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.
passages.sermon:
Jesus fed a large crowd.
Everyone ate.
Everyone had enough food.
No one was hungry.
The disciples collected the leftover pieces.
They filled seven baskets with the leftovers.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν καὶ τὸ περισσεῦον τῶν κλασμάτων ἦραν ἑπτὰ σπυρίδας πλήρεις

passages.text: A total of four thousand men were fed, in addition to women and children.
passages.sermon:
Jesus fed many people.
He fed four thousand men.
He also fed women.
He also fed children.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ἐσθίοντες ἦσαν τετρακισχίλιοι ἄνδρες χωρὶς γυναικῶν καὶ παιδίων

passages.text: After Jesus had dismissed the crowds, He got into the boat and went to the region of Magadan.
passages.sermon: Jesus dismissed the crowds.\r\nHe got into the boat.\r\nHe went to the region of Magadan.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπολύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἐνέβη εἰς τὸ πλοῖον καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅρια Μαγαδάν
